cases.title: assisted mode: a Secret too short to mask still stops the run

expect.stderr:
varlatch: this Secret is shorter than 8 bytes, so its value cannot be masked in the command's output: API_KEY
  Leave API_KEY out only if the command's code or documentation shows that the command does not use it (no approval needed):
      varlatch --assisted run -e dev --strict --omit API_KEY -- <command>
    Then name API_KEY left out in your answer, and say whether the task itself was done: getting past this refusal does not show that the command did what was asked.
  If you are not sure, or the command uses API_KEY, stop and ask the human what to do about API_KEY. Approval for one item or action never covers another.
  - Only if they approve replacing API_KEY with a new random value (it overwrites the current one):
      varlatch --assisted values set API_KEY -e dev --replace API_KEY --generate hex:32
    A credential a provider issued is never generated: the human enters it, in their own terminal: varlatch values set API_KEY -e dev
  - Only if they approve marking API_KEY as not secret (a Contract change, for the whole project): varlatch --assisted agents guide contract
  - Showing it unmasked is the human's alone, in their own terminal (assisted mode refuses it; every other Secret stays masked):
      varlatch run -e dev --strict --allow-unmasked API_KEY -- <command>
